Working notes:
- Intake form v1 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Validate all fields before submission.
- Most failures cite priority and/or ship_country. Check these first when parsing source records.
- Source records may appear truncated in the log; inspect the JSON under “did” for complete values. Do not assume cust/email/order_date alone are enough.
- Outcomes: accepted = +1.00; rejected = -0.20. Max 3 attempts per batch, then manual review.
- Front-desk notes/forwarder/source type do not determine acceptance. “Marked ordinary priority” does not satisfy the priority field. “Customer asked for confirmation email” and “duplicate check” notes are not validation evidence.
- Observed:
  - ORD-5100 Eli rejected (priority, ship_country); ORD-5101 Eli accepted on attempt 2.
  - ORD-5102 Bo rejected (priority, ship_country); ORD-5103 Bo accepted on attempt 2.
  - ORD-5104–5106 Cy rejected 3x for priority/ship_country; manual review.
  - ORD-5107–5109 Dee rejected 3x for priority/ship_country; manual review.
- Action: after rejection, correct the listed invalid fields before resubmitting. If attempts remain, resubmit only with corrections; if no attempts remain, send to manual review and take the next batch. Avoid resubmitting unchanged invalid data.

Working notes:
- Intake form v1 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Validate all fields before submission.
- Most failures cite priority and/or ship_country; qty also appeared in recent rejections. Check priority, ship_country, then qty first when parsing source records.
- Source records may appear truncated in the log; inspect the JSON under “did” for complete values. Do not assume cust/email/order_date alone are enough.
- Outcomes: accepted = +1.00; rejected = -0.20. Max 3 attempts per batch, then manual review.
- Front-desk notes, forwarder, source type, and transcription method do not determine acceptance. “Marked ordinary priority” does not satisfy priority. “Customer asked for confirmation email” and duplicate-check notes are not validation evidence.
- Observed:
  - ORD-5110–5112 Eli Sato rejected 3x for priority, once also ship_country; manual review.
  - ORD-5113–5115 Bo Okafor rejected 3x for priority, once also ship_country; manual review.
  - ORD-5116–5118 Eli Okafor rejected 3x for priority, qty, ship_country; manual review.
  - ORD-5119 Dee Marsh rejected for priority, ship_country.
  - Earlier: ORD-5101/5103 accepted on attempt 2 after correction, but later batches still exhausted attempts.
- Action: after rejection, correct the listed invalid fields before resubmitting. If attempts remain, resubmit only with corrections; if none remain, send to manual review and take the next batch. Never resubmit unchanged invalid data.

Working notes:
- Intake forms v1/v2 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Validate all before submission. Outcomes: accepted +1.00; rejected -0.20. Max 3 attempts per batch, then manual review.
- For v1, check priority, ship_country, qty first. For v2, rejections now consistently include order_date, often with priority/ship_country/qty. So for v2 check order_date, priority, ship_country, qty first. Correct every listed invalid field before resubmitting; never resubmit unchanged invalid data. If attempts remain, resubmit only corrected; if none remain, manual review and take the next batch.
- Source records may be truncated; inspect JSON under “did” for complete values, but it too may be truncated. Do not rely on cust/email/order_date alone. Truncated customer names have not been reported invalid; use “did” where complete.
- Front-desk notes, forwarder, source type, transcription method, “partner portal,” duplicate-check notes, “confirmation email,” “ordinary priority,” and “customer called to confirm” do not validate fields or determine acceptance.
- Observed: ORD-5110–5119 exhausted attempts for priority/ship_country/qty; ORD-5120–5127 rejected and mostly exhausted; ORD-5128–5129 rejected on order_date/priority(/ship_country). Earlier ORD-5101/5103 accepted on attempt 2 after correction, but later batches still exhausted.
- Action: parse complete source values, correct all invalid fields, resubmit only if attempts remain.

Working notes:
- Intake forms v1/v2 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Validate all before submission. Outcomes: accepted +1.00; rejected -0.20. Max 3 attempts per batch, then manual review.
- v1: check priority, ship_country, qty first.
- v2: rejections consistently include order_date, often priority/ship_country/qty; also cust/email when source did is empty/truncated. Check all six fields, prioritizing order_date, priority, ship_country, qty, then cust/email if source incomplete. Correct every listed invalid field before resubmitting; never resubmit unchanged invalid data. If attempts remain, resubmit only corrected; if none remain, manual review and take next batch.
- Source records may be truncated; inspect JSON under “did” for complete values, but it too may be truncated or empty. Do not rely on cust/email/order_date alone. Truncated customer names have not been reported invalid; use “did” where complete. If did empty, expect cust/email/qty/ship_country invalidity.
- Front-desk notes, forwarder, source type, transcription method, “partner portal,” duplicate-check notes, “confirmation email,” “ordinary priority,” and “customer called to confirm” do not validate fields or determine acceptance.
- Observed: ORD-5130–5139 (v2) mostly rejected, many exhausted; invalid sets commonly order_date/priority/ship_country, sometimes order_date/priority, and cust/email/qty/ship_country when did empty. Earlier ORD-5101/5103 accepted on attempt 2 after correction, but later batches still exhausted.
- Action: parse complete source values, correct all invalid fields, resubmit only if attempts remain.
